deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematical derivations. It is a sequence of aphorisms separated by short horizontal rules, continuing the reflective notes of the previous page and running on into the next. In order:

(1) A bad mathematical-physical theory is like a dismantled rattletrap cart ("demontirtes Rumpelfuhrwerk") that must be set upright again every 3 minutes so that it keeps going ("Kinderspielzeug"). The word "mathematisch" is inserted above the line.

(2) No knowledge at all is often preferable to half and blurred knowledge, because the latter harms character and intelligence, especially in young people.

(3) A definition: spatial intuition (Raumanschauung) is to have space before the senses without its being before the senses.

(4) Cantor's set theory is perhaps the most profound thing ("das tiefsinnigste") that human beings have ever thought.

(5) It would be dreadful if the mathematician existed merely to compute the problems the physicist needs.

(6) People know much more than they write. The best of what they know they do not write, though sometimes they write more than they know.

(7) A reworded version of (1): many mathematical-physical theories seem to him like a child's toy that has fallen into disorder ("Un" of "Unordnung" inserted above the line) and must be set up again every 3 minutes to keep going.

(8) There is not only a geometric intuition but also an arithmetic one, a third kind (reading uncertain, probably "künstlerische", artistic), and a psychological or physiological one. He cites Helmholtz, Vorträge und Reden I, pp. 173-174, where the word "Anschauung" occurs once on each page. He then glosses Anschauung as rapid, unconscious combining that is not definitively certain-logical. The sentence beginning "Vielleicht" continues on the next page (freehand drawing, auditive thinking as one-dimensional).

Nothing here can be reconstructed in modern notation. The content belongs to Hilbert's views on intuition versus logic, the autonomy of mathematics from physics, and his admiration for Cantor.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible, since the page contains no computations.
Aphorisms (1) and (7) are two drafts of the same simile. The second, with 'in Unordnung geraten', looks like a reformulation of the first.

deep.surprise_reason: These are personal aphorisms consistent with well-documented Hilbert views: his admiration of Cantor, his reflections on Anschauung, and his insistence on the autonomy of mathematics. The exact wording ('das tiefsinnigste') and the toy simile are nice unpublished details for a historian. They contain no mathematical result.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'demontirten Rumpelfuhrwerk, der alle 3 Minuten' is probably 'das alle 3 Minuten' (the neuter relative pronoun fits the noun). The hand is ambiguous; keep as uncertain.
'wenn der Mathematiker [-...-] bloss': the struck fragment looks like a false start 'bo' or 'bloss' crossed out before 'bloss'.
'eine mechanische [?]' is more likely 'eine künstlerische'. The letter shapes (K-ü-n-s-t-l-e-r-i-s-c-h-e) and the Helmholtz reference (artistic induction in Vorträge und Reden I) both support this.
'physiologische Anschauung' may be 'psychologische Anschauung'. The handwriting ('phycholo-gische') and Helmholtz's 'psychologischer Takt' in the cited passage favour 'psychologische'. Uncertain.
'd.h. das rasche, unbewusste, nicht definitiv sicher-logische Combiniren': the struck word before 'd.h.' reads approximately 'Daraus' or 'Das ist'; illegible beyond that.
